column1: # Which committed run feeds which published destination.
# One row per published output. The generator reads this file; nothing in
# scripts/bench-report.py names a run directory, an endpoint or a page any more.
# That is the point: the choice of data source was previously three string
# constants scattered through the generator plus nineteen test assertions, so
# re-pointing a page meant editing code in several places and finding out
# afterwards which page silently changed.
# Columns, tab separated. `#` starts a comment, blank lines are ignored, and the
# header row is the first non-comment line.
#   destination  which published output this row configures. One of:
#                  docs       the volucer documentation page (12-BENCHMARKS.md)
#                  homepage   the two-or-more charts the Sailantis landing page embeds
#   run          the directory under results/ holding matrix.tsv and memory.tsv
#   endpoints    the pages the destination draws, comma separated, in reading
#                order. Use `*` for "whatever the run measured". A destination
#                that pools rows (docs) must name exactly one, because it keys
#                every figure on arm/workers/opcache/conc and a second endpoint
#                would satisfy that key for a different amount of work.
#   mode         the opcache mode the rows must carry (`on`) — the run's own
#                column, so a JIT-on and a JIT-off pass cannot be mixed.
#   required     whether a missing run is an error (`yes`) or a skip (`no`).
#   note         why this run, for the next person who is tempted to re-point it
destination
docs
column6: Single-endpoint pass, so the pooled medians describe one page. Second pass of the scale grid: the first carried a volucer-worker decline that did not reproduce.
